node-1.label: 9-year-old girl has thickened nails and keratinized plaques on palms, soles, and corners of mouth since birth

node-2.label: At age 1, fingernails and toenails began to turn yellow and thicken; skin of stressed parts of palms and soles gradually became keratinized, thickened, black and chapped.

node-3.label: No family history of similar symptoms.

node-4.label: Nail examination: fingernails and toenails partly thickened and raised in wedge shape, surface rough, opaque, and dirty brown; skin examination: dry skin on trunk and extremities, punctate and flaky keratinized dark brown thickened patches on palms and soles; oral examination: fissured tongue, oral leukokeratosis, and keratotic plaques in corners of mouth.

node-5.label: Physical examination showed normal vision, hearing, intelligence, and growth with moderate nutrition; no natal teeth, follicular sebaceous cysts, hair loss, or other organ abnormalities.

why.why: Genetic testing identified a heterozygous KRT6A c.1460-2_1460del variant that is absent in both parents, confirming a de novo mutation diagnostic of Pachyonychia congenita, a congenital hereditary keratoderma. The clinical triad of nail dystrophy, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, and oral leukokeratosis matches this diagnosis. Pathologist and laboratory physician analyses agree that molecular confirmation is sufficient even without skin biopsy, so confidence rises from 0.75 to 0.98.

The newly confirmed KRT6A mutation establishes a specific hereditary keratoderma (Pachyonychia congenita) rather than a multisystem ectodermal dysplasia. The patient's normal hair, teeth, and intelligence remain incompatible with the broad ectodermal dysplasia phenotype, and expert analyses support the keratoderma diagnosis. Confidence is therefore reduced from 0.20 to 0.05.

Detection of a de novo KRT6A mutation provides a definitive genetic cause for the congenital nail, skin, and oral mucosal changes, excluding an acquired chronic inflammatory dermatosis. The congenital onset and oral leukokeratosis also argue against inflammation. Pathologist and laboratory analyses confirm this genetic etiology, so confidence is lowered from 0.05 to 0.01.

node-10.label: Parental genetic testing is negative for the KRT6A variant in both parents, indicating a de novo mutation

why.why: Both laboratory and pathological expert analyses independently confirm that the heterozygous KRT6A c.1460-2_1460del variant, validated by whole-exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing and absent in both parents, is diagnostic for Pachyonychia congenita. The clinical triad is fully concordant, and even without skin biopsy or imaging the molecular evidence is considered sufficient. This raises confidence from 0.97 to 0.98.
